name: Lido on Solana (stSOL) Withdrawal Bug
architecture: Liquid staking token (stSOL) program mid-way through a governance-approved sunset and migration away from Solana.
rootCause: Following an October 2023 DAO vote to wind down Lido on Solana, the web frontend for unstaking was removed in February 2024 and holders were directed to a CLI-based unstaking flow. A bug in the unstaking/withdrawal contract logic then prevented affected stSOL holders from redeeming through that path.
fundLockMechanism: The withdrawal path itself failed during a protocol state transition (active staking -> sunset/wind-down): the code path holders were told to use to exit stopped working, with no alternative redemption route offered at the time.

amount.note: Our design references originally sketched this incident at ~$38M; independent reporting we could verify (dlnews.com, Feb 2024) puts the affected balance at over 112,000 stSOL worth more than $24M at the time. We use the sourced figure, not the earlier placeholder.

recoveryAttempts: The Lido-on-Solana operating team (P2P) continued working on the wind-down process after the bug was reported; holders pursued CLI-based unstaking as the intended remaining path. We did not find a dated public confirmation that every affected holder was made whole, so we do not claim full resolution.

primarySources.title: Broken code traps $24m of Lido staked SOL — and holders want their tokens back

limitations: Solana/stSOL is outside FLARE's currently implemented EVM/Solidity analyzer (the Solana adapter is an interface-only stub — see docs/LIMITATIONS.md); this case study is documentation-only and cannot be reproduced through the FLARE engine today. We could not confirm a precise final resolution date or whether 100% of affected balances were ultimately recovered.
